title: AerCap / Aerie Pharmaceuticals / Aeromexico / AES — Price, Tail Risk, Security Payoff and Observable Catalysts V9

notes: AES 2020 raw Short -> actual Long; original text explicitly presents a $32 upside target and bullish catalyst stack.
AerCap 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2022 existing short-form canonical files were upgraded in place to V9 rather than duplicated.
AERI 2016 is genuinely a Short. The terminal outcome is Alcon's $15.25/share cash acquisition; no source-DB performance row is available.
Grupo Aeromexico 2017 has no source-DB performance row. Chapter 11 treatment is decisive: legacy equity received less than 0.01% of reorganized equity.

AerCap 2022 suffered a Russia-related pre-tax net charge of about $2.7bn shortly after publication. Later book-value and insurance-recovery gains are classified as delayed recovery, not as success within the original one-year path.
AerCap vintages are kept separate because entry P/B, liquidity state, acquisition state and tail-risk regime differ materially.

batch_lessons: The same company can be a mediocre investment near book and an exceptional one at 0.4x book because the implied permanent impairment is different.
Book-value growth and terminal P/B are separate forecasts; getting the first right does not guarantee stock returns.
Aircraft-lessor underwriting should compare near-term maturities and purchase commitments with actual liquidity and covenant headroom.
Contracted lease revenue does not eliminate airline solvency or collection risk.
Global leased assets require jurisdictional and physical-recovery stress tests, not only legal-title analysis.
A fundamentally accurate biotech short can still lose because regulatory success and strategic M&A value dominate the equity payoff.
A strategic shareholder's historic purchase price is not a bankruptcy floor for common equity.
Non-recourse project debt can reduce corporate distress risk without ensuring parent-level EPS growth.
Transformation theses are strongest when they contain observable milestones such as backlog, credit-rating upgrades, mix shifts and external asset valuations.
Original-horizon failure and delayed recovery must remain separate labels.
